minimal_context: The student is asked to explain an academic concept in English during a Grade 10 CLIL lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I have just spent some time explaining the three main stages of the water cycle. Now, I want you to explain the first stage, evaporation, in your own words.

STUDENT: Um... yes. The water... it gets hot.

TUTOR: What else can you tell me about it?

STUDENT: Ah... the sun... the sun makes the water... um... change.

TUTOR: Please continue.

STUDENT: So... um... it... the water is... ah... it becomes... um... gas. And... ah... it... it goes up. That's... um... all.

options.A: Provide time for individual, pair, or group work before nominating the student to give a response (e.g., Think, Pair, Share).
options.B: Describe the inappropriate behavior using objective, behavioral terms, and detail the antecedent events that led up to the displayed misbehavior.
options.C: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., a high five or thumbs up) indicating approval of the response beyond simple acknowledgment.
options.D: Terminate the demand to explain the water cycle and remove the instructional materials from the student for 10 seconds.
